It's important to understand that traffic is regional.  Perhaps you know this, but for others, if there are no downloads in a region, then that region gets 0 traffic.  AP folks know this very well.  Rewards are determined by traffic share, globally not regionally.

Part of the "Node game" is positioning yourself regionally where the traffic flows.  Traffic has been dominant in the US/NA region over the past 2 months. Before that,  EU dominated for many months. During those months, US was the worst place to be.  AP always has a mixture of 0 days and large days (per Node).

A couple of days with little to no traffic in the US/NA region isn't cause for alarm. It could mean the tide is changing again.  Welcome to the Node game!   (edited)

I need to upgrade my nodes to the latest version in Docker, is there any tutorial how to manage this ?

Hello,  I assume you are running a Pool.  If so, the commands below will do it.  If not, it's the Pool Operator you have delegated to who must handle it.   Also, there is an Operators channel for Pool Operators.  That's the better place for this discussion in the future.  You can open a ticket to request access if you don't already have it, again assuming you are a Pool Operator.

docker compose down  - might not need to do this, but it's safe
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d

If you are using linux, you can chain them together.  Not sure if there is an equivalent Windows chain. 

docker compose down && docker compose pull && docker compose up -d

Spin up Virtual Machines to spike downloads?

Do people create their own traffic?  Yes. I do it now and then in AP to retain my delegators there.  If we have a couple of zero days, I toss a download in to get some traffic and try to even things out a bit.

Do we have a problem with constant abuse?  Not at the moment.  The recent organic activity from the releases has demotivated most if not all from the practice.  When we had many months between releases, I think most of the traffic was artificial.  I was generating more then as well, to survive and in some sense battle others doing the same.  It's rarely been out of control and generally respectful by all though from my observation.

The past week there has simply been low traffic in all regions.  That's what happens between releases and when there is no player growth.  Nothing happening recently is due to abuse of the system as far as I can tell.  It's a normal cycle given the state of the project.

The IR team monitors this activity.  They know what is going on.  Every download, every byte is tracked to the user who is logged in and downloading.   They can reach out to anyone they see abusing the system.  They probably have the ability to cut them off as well. 

A few of us have developed our own tracking of activity hitting our servers by IP address.  We can tell if a lot of traffic is coming from the same place.  My dashboard is public. Link in my profile. (edited)
